title: Code Quality and Static Analysis
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of code quality and static analysis and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—compiler warnings—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study code quality and static analysis with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you reduce a failure to a reproducible cause and capture evidence without leaking sensitive data. In this lesson, focus on compiler warnings and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A useful debugging workflow reproduces the issue, narrows the suspected cause, and records evidence. Logs and diagnostics should explain system behavior without leaking secrets or personal data. Apply that reasoning specifically to compiler warnings and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect compiler warnings with checkstyle or comparable style tools before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Reproduce the state, inspect one variable or stack frame, and retest after a focused change. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: design a check for code quality and static analysis that includes a normal case, a boundary case, and a failure case. Make the check fail visibly when the behavior is wrong.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates at least one listed topic from Code Quality and Static Analysis.
The learner states the expected result before running or inspecting the example.
At least one boundary, failure, compatibility, or maintainability consideration is documented where relevant.
hints: Start by identifying the contract or rule behind compiler warnings.
Reduce the example to the smallest input that makes the behavior visible.
Test one boundary or failure case and compare the result with the expected behavior.
content.execution_notes: Java requires a JDK or a separate isolated server runner. No Java sandbox is bundled with this content; never execute learner code inside the FastAPI process or public production container.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.

summary: Code Quality and Static Analysis is best understood by connecting its contract to a small observable example.
Key syllabus points: Compiler warnings, Checkstyle or comparable style tools, SpotBugs or comparable bug detection.
Use official versioned documentation and tests to confirm assumptions before relying on behavior in a larger application.
